subject.title: Bounded memory tool with hard character limits

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class bounded memory CRUD write contract to memory-core, and what hard-limit, identity, duplicate/consolidation, config, snapshot, and secret-handling semantics should it expose?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but implementing it would create a new public memory-write API plus security, persistence, and upgrade behavior that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Define memory-core bounded CRUD
options.body: Adopt this as a memory-core design track and specify add/list/replace/remove, capacity feedback, limit enforcement, identity, duplicate handling, snapshot semantics, and secret policy before code lands.

options.title: Narrow to existing memory maintenance paths
options.body: Keep first-class CRUD out of core for now and address bloat through memory-flush, promotion, diagnostics, and recall surfaces only.

options.title: Route to plugin experimentation
options.body: Ask contributors to prototype the write policy as a memory plugin or ClawHub package until a core/plugin API gap is proven.

recommendation.title: Define memory-core bounded CRUD
recommendation.body: Adopt this as a memory-core design track and specify add/list/replace/remove, capacity feedback, limit enforcement, identity, duplicate handling, snapshot semantics, and secret policy before code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans memory-core public tools, persistence, and plugin-boundary semantics, and steipete has strong visible feature-history signals in those paths.
